deepdive.thesis: SIS delivered record Q4FY26 revenue (INR 4,489 cr, +31% YoY) and EBITDA (INR 207 cr, 4.6% margin) driven by APS consolidation and event-driven international spikes, signaling a structural inflection as new Labour Codes neutralize compliance arbitrage for unorganized competitors. While the Cash IPO is deferred to FY27 due to market conditions, the core security/FM platform is compounding at >15% with ROCE now exceeding 16.5%, validating the '15x15' growth-return framework.

open.item: Management flags that the Labour Codes transition, including implementation and contract resets across the customer base, will take time to fully unfold, spanning the next 4-6 quarters, with the impact varying by quarter along the way.

Group Managing Director set out 'Vision 2030', a strategic framework with two objectives: continuing to expand market share across operating segments, and steadily raising the 'solutions quotient' of the business (the share of revenue from integrated, technology-enabled, outcome-led solutions rather than manpower alone), via investment in AI-enabled video surveillance, integrated command centers, mechanized/automated facility management, and digitally instrumented service delivery.

Vision 2030 sets two objectives — continue expanding market share across existing segments, and steadily raise the 'solutions quotient' (technology-enabled solutions share of revenue) — described as a transition from a manpower-led services company to a technology-enabled solutions company operating at scale.

The IPO of the cash logistics business (held via the SIS Cash Services joint-venture structure) is deferred, not abandoned; the DRHP is filed and the regulatory pathway is well advanced, with management intending to proceed when market conditions support the desired outcome.

Management expects further value from the AP Securitas acquisition through cost optimization and operating leverage between the two customer franchises, with synergy benefits expected to compound over the next few years.

MSS Security will complete the nationwide rollout of its Workforce rostering and time-and-attendance system, building on the previously deployed Workday HRMS platform, and continue investments in tender-management, costing, and contract-billing systems.

MSS Security will focus on scaling technology-led capabilities, including remote AI-based monitoring, drones, and integrated command-center solutions, alongside enhancing operational efficiencies through workforce optimization and digital systems, while expanding presence in healthcare, aged care, emergency response, and non-emergency patient transport services and deepening penetration of Tier 1 airports, data centers, public transport, and government/critical infrastructure markets.

The Company is committed to robust organic growth while selectively pursuing inorganic opportunities to accelerate market expansion and capabilities, continuing to evaluate acquisitions with niche capabilities and customer segments that can augment service offerings or presence, especially in the India businesses.

MSS will also pursue strategic acquisitions, strengthen leadership capabilities, and continue advancing innovation, cyber resilience, ESG priorities, and compliance excellence to reinforce its position as a trusted and future-ready integrated services provider.

risks.note: The business depends on consistent process, systems and workforce execution across a workforce of over 3 lakh employees deployed across multiple geographies and thousands of customer sites; failures in recruitment, training, deployment, supervision or performance management can directly impact service quality and client retention.
risks.risk: Operational/execution risk inherent to a labour-intensive services model

risks.note: Operational risk is influenced by labour availability, attrition, and wage inflation across geographies, and by the operational transition associated with regulatory changes in workforce frameworks (e.g., the new Labour Codes and periodic minimum-wage revisions), which is increasing human resource costs Pan-India even though most customer contracts allow proportionate price pass-through.
risks.risk: Labour availability, attrition and wage inflation, amplified by workforce-regulation transitions

risks.note: The Group's increasing reliance on technology platforms (SISCORE, Oracle ERP, Shared Services Centre, digitized attendance and compliance systems) for service delivery, financial reporting, workforce management and customer interface exposes it to IT/cyber risk; management responded during FY26 with an Identity & Access Management rollout, MFA/PAM/ZTNA deployment, encrypted backups, VAPT exercises, a cyber-attack simulation, and disaster-recovery testing, indicating this is an actively managed but material exposure.
risks.risk: Information technology and cyber security risk

risks.note: The Group operates in a highly regulated environment spanning labour laws, licensing, taxation and industry-specific regulation across India, Australia, New Zealand and Singapore; variation in regulatory interpretation and enforcement across regions can expose the business to compliance-related risk, managed via a centralized Compliance Tool and quarterly Board reporting.
risks.risk: Legal, compliance and regulatory risk across multiple jurisdictions

risks.note: The Group's risk framework explicitly integrates a structured approach to managing risks arising from mergers, acquisitions and business integration - including pre-transaction due diligence, integration planning and post-acquisition monitoring - reflecting the elevated integration risk from recent and planned acquisitions such as AP Securitas and MSS's State Medical Assistance.
risks.risk: M&A and business-integration risk from the continued inorganic growth agenda

risks.note: Labour shortages across international geographies (Australia, New Zealand, Singapore) continued to have an impact on costs during FY26, a structural constraint on margins in the Security Solutions - International segment.
risks.risk: International labour shortages raising cost pressure

risks.note: Heightened global geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East/Israel-Iran conflict, Russia-Ukraine conflict, West Asia energy crisis, tariff tensions and trade-policy uncertainty) is flagged as a risk to the economic outlook across India and Australia, with potential to pressure operating costs (energy, freight, insurance) and inflation even though it is not viewed as directly disrupting demand for security/FM services.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty affecting the broader operating environment
